title: Antimicrobial Resistance

segments.say: For eighty years, a few pills could cure infections that once killed. Now some germs are learning to shrug those pills off.
An antibiotic kills most of the bacteria. But a few, by chance, survive. They multiply, and the next time, the drug doesn't work. That is antimicrobial resistance.
We speed it up. Antibiotics taken for colds, which are viral. Courses stopped halfway. Drugs fed to farm animals. And dirty water that spreads resistant germs.
These are MRSA bacteria, which resist many common antibiotics. Hospitals around the world fight them every day.

anim.title: Deaths caused directly by resistant infections, 2019

segments.say: In twenty nineteen, resistant infections directly caused about one point two seven million deaths worldwide. The World Health Organization counts it among the top global health threats.

anim.title: India's response
items: Red line on packs of prescription-only antibiotics

segments.say: India made a national action plan in twenty seventeen. Packs of prescription-only antibiotics carry a red line, a reminder not to take them without a doctor.
For Prelims and GS: misuse selects resistant germs. Fighting it needs one approach for people, animals and the environment together: One Health.

sources: WHO fact sheet, 'Antimicrobial resistance' (2023): AMR is one of the top global public health threats; bacterial AMR was directly responsible for 1.27 million global deaths in 2019
GRAM study, The Lancet, 2022: 1.27 million deaths attributable to bacterial AMR in 2019
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance (2017–2021), One Health approach; 'Red Line' campaign (2016) on prescription-only antibiotic packs
Government of Kerala, Kerala Antimicrobial Resistance Strategic Action Plan (KARSAP), 2018: first state-level plan

quiz.q: Why are antibiotics useless against a common cold?
quiz.why: Antibiotics act on bacteria; colds are viral.

quiz.q: What does the red line on some medicine packs mean?
options: Prescription-only antibiotic: take only on a doctor's advice
quiz.why: The Red Line campaign marks prescription-only antibiotics.

quiz.q: Which approach links human, animal and environmental health?
quiz.why: AMR plans use the One Health approach.

reviewNote: Facts were read against WHO's AMR fact sheet, the 2022 Lancet GRAM study, India's 2017 National Action Plan and Kerala's KARSAP. Tone is serious: one death figure, no music, no drama. Microscope images are CDC/NIAID. Moving facts: newer estimates may update the 2019 figure.
